explanation: A dial over English prose whose main trigger (0.5-1.0 of max) is a cardinal quantity right before a counted noun: a number word from two to ten or a small digit ('has 3 bells', 'three children and two dogs', 'five apples', 'four sisters', 'No. 3', '3 games to 2') or a middle ordinal ('third place', 'the fourth time'); 'first', 'last', 'some', 'many', 'no', years, and chapter, page or code digits stay under about 0.35. Apart from that, the first '.' token of a text gives a fixed ~0.45 whatever its role (sentence end, 'Dr.', '2.0'), while '!', '?' and later full stops stay near 0.1; a weak 0.25-0.45 band covers 'was'/'has' right after an opening pronoun ('It was', 'He has'), the 'of' in 'one of', and motion or posture verbs with their path preposition ('lay', 'flew across', 'returned to'); clauses with no '.' and no numeral about tastes, opinions, weather or routines ('My brother enjoys cooking pasta', 'The weather seems nice today', 'I think this idea is great'), questions, imperatives and short code stay below 0.25.
